hints: A move splits a pile into two positive piles of different sizes.
For each total size, mark it winning if any allowed unequal split leaves two losing positions.
Both resulting piles are independent games, so their Grundy values combine by XOR.
analogy: Try every legal unequal split; a move is winning when it leaves no winning continuation for the opponent.
example: A pile of 1 has no legal split and is losing; pile 4 can split 1+3, but those states decide its outcome.
algorithm: Precompute win[0..N]. For each s, test unequal splits a<s-a; s is winning if both win[a] and win[s-a] are false. Stop at the first such split. Use a bitset of losing positions to test partner s-a quickly; the input bound is N=1,000,000.
correctness: A move is winning exactly when it leaves both resulting heaps in losing positions; all splits are tried, and equal splits are forbidden by the rules.
complexity: O(N^2/wordSize) bitset work in the worst case and O(N) memory; practical precomputation checks losing positions in parallel.
